services.name: AdminService
services.comment:
Running the platform: counts, the audit log, the cluster policies the
console keeps current, and the catalog it registers from. Admins only.

methods.name: GetStats
methods.comment: Platform-wide counts, for the admin home page.

methods.name: ListAuditEntries
methods.comment:
Every request that tried to change something, allowed or refused,
newest first: who, what, what it named (never a secret value, password
or token) and the outcome.

methods.name: ListAuditReads
methods.comment:
Who read a run's outputs, failure messages or logs, or a team's secret
names, newest first: who, by which method, and what they read, by name
only (never the content). Reading it is itself recorded.

methods.name: GetPolicySync
methods.comment:
Whether the cluster's policies are current: the last outcome of
rewriting each from the console's database.

methods.name: SyncPolicies
methods.comment: Rewrites them now.

methods.name: GetCatalogStatus
methods.comment:
The catalog release this console last applied (teams, products and
SecretStores), what it couldn't apply, and how its last look went.

methods.name: SyncCatalog
methods.comment:
Reads the catalog's release now, and applies it, even if it's the one
already applied. The console also looks every few minutes by itself.

methods.name: AdoptCatalogTeam
methods.comment:
Lets the catalog's release manage a team it didn't make (one made by
hand, or before this console read releases), then syncs. Until then a
release that names such a team leaves it, its products and its
SecretStores alone: a new catalog folder never takes over an existing
team's namespace and secrets unless an admin says so.

methods.name: GetInstall
methods.comment:
This install: the console's version, and which of its optional parts
are on (each set in vennir.yaml, or the console chart's values).

services.name: ApiService
services.comment:
API products (decision 20): a backend a team already runs, published
through this install's gateway. Its OpenAPI file is the allowlist: the
gateway forwards only requests whose method and path are an operation
there and that fit its schemas, and blocks everything else. An API comes
from its team's catalog (apis/<name>/api.yaml); pausing one is the only
change made here.

Everyone signed in sees the APIs that aren't hidden; they may call one
(may_call) when it's their own team's, when it's granted to them or to a
single sign-on group they're in, or, for this release, when its
api.yaml's shareWith names one of their teams (decision 26). The
backend's address and how the gateway signs in there are shown to the
API's own team only.

Access (decision 26): each API has grants, to a group (each person in it)
or to one user (a person or a bot), each with its rate. Only the API's
team's maintainers add grants or change their rates. A person asks for
access for themselves, offering none or some of their groups; a
maintainer of a bot's team asks for the bot. The API's maintainers
approve (granting the person, or one of the groups they offered) or
decline. Revoking: the API's maintainers, an admin, the
person a grant names, or the maintainers of the bot it names. Every
change is audited and told to whoever it's for and the API's maintainers.

methods.name: ListApis
methods.comment: Every API the caller may see, by team and name.

methods.name: GetApi
methods.comment: One API, with its OpenAPI document. Not found and hidden look the same.

methods.name: PauseApi
methods.comment:
Stops an API for an incident: every signed-in caller gets 503 with its
message (anyone else, 404) until it's resumed, and nothing reaches the
backend. A maintainer of its team, or an admin.

methods.name: ResumeApi
methods.comment: Lets a paused API through again; as PauseApi.

methods.name: GetApiTraffic
methods.comment:
What callers sent an API, what the gateway stopped and what its
backend answered, over the last hours (at most a week): by endpoint,
the requests its spec doesn't describe, and by calling team. Its own
team, and admins.

methods.name: GetGateway
methods.comment:
The gateway's settings (this install's Helm values), whether it's
closed, and what it refused at the door over the last day. Admins.

methods.name: SetGatewayClosed
methods.comment:
Closes the gateway (a message: every API answers 503 with it, and
nothing is forwarded) or reopens it (empty). Admins; audited.

methods.name: RequestApiAccess
methods.comment:
Asks for access to an API, with a reason: a person for themselves, or a
maintainer of a bot's team for that bot (bot_email). Refused when its
api.yaml takes no requests (access.requests: closed), when whoever
it's for may call it already (but only "from the catalog", by its
api.yaml's shareWith: then a grant may be asked for), or while a
request of theirs waits. An API whose requests are open grants it at
once, at its default limit.

methods.name: WithdrawApiAccessRequest
methods.comment:
Withdraws a request while it waits: whoever asked, or, for a bot's, a
maintainer of one of the bot's teams that isn't retired.

methods.name: DecideApiAccessRequest
methods.comment:
Grants (approve) or declines a waiting request: a maintainer of the
API's team. Granting a person may grant one of the groups they offered
instead (and only those); a bot is granted by name only.

methods.name: AddApiGrant
methods.comment:
Grants a group or a user (a person or a bot, by email) access: a
maintainer of the API's team (not an admin, unless they maintain it).

methods.name: SetApiGrantRate
methods.comment: Changes a grant's rate: a maintainer of the API's team.

methods.name: RevokeApiGrant
methods.comment:
Revokes a grant: a maintainer of the API's team, an admin, the person
it names, or a maintainer of the bot's team it names. The gateway stops
its calls within its refresh (well under a minute).

methods.name: ListApiAccess
methods.comment:
An API's grants (active and revoked) and requests: its own team, and
admins.

methods.name: ListMyApiAccess
methods.comment:
The APIs the caller may call, and how (their team's, granted to them,
through a group, from the catalog), and their requests that wait or
were declined.

methods.name: ListTeamBotApiAccess
methods.comment: A team's bots' grants and requests: its members, and admins.

methods.name: ListAwayApiAccess
methods.comment:
The grants and requests of a team's APIs that left the catalog's
release (away_since): kept 30 days, to come back with an API of the
same name, and revocable meanwhile by the team's maintainers and
admins. Its members, and admins.

methods.name: ListAllApiGrants
methods.comment:
Every active grant on this install, newest first, a page at a time:
published APIs' and away ones' (away_since), for an incident (an admin
revokes; the APIs' teams add and change them). With how many there are
of each kind, and the requests waiting. Admins.

services.name: AuthService
services.comment:
Signing in, and who you are. Bots don't sign in: they send their API
token as the bearer token directly.

methods.name: GetEnvironment
methods.comment: Which deployment this is. Anyone, signed in or not.

methods.name: Register
methods.comment:
Creates your own account, when open registration is on (off by
default: admins create accounts with UserService.CreateUser).

methods.name: Login
methods.comment:
Returns a session token. Rate limited per client and per email, and
spaced out after repeated failures on one account (resource_exhausted,
with a Retry-After).

methods.name: ExchangeToken
methods.comment:
Signs a bot in with its CI's own OIDC identity instead of a stored
token (keyless): a GitHub Actions or GitLab job's ID token, for this
install's audience, matching exactly one bot's identity
(TokenService.AddBotIdentity). Returns an hour's session as that bot.
Refused (unauthenticated, KEYLESS_REFUSED) otherwise.

methods.name: GetMe
methods.comment: Who you are, and your teams.

methods.name: ChangePassword
methods.comment:
Changes your password (people only), signing out your other sessions;
returns a fresh token for this one.

methods.name: SignOut
methods.comment:
Ends this session: its token is refused from now on, by the console
and the gateway. An API token is revoked with TokenService.RevokeToken
instead.

services.name: ChatService
services.comment:
The chat agent (decision 24): answers from the docs and the catalog,
looks at what the person's teams have, and proposes carts, all as the
signed-in person, through the console's own checks. It never orders: a
cart it proposes is the person's to open and place.

methods.name: GetChatSettings
methods.comment: Whether chat is on here, and with which model.

methods.name: Ask
methods.comment:
An answer to the conversation's last message. Nothing is kept: send
the conversation each time. CHAT_OFF without a model here;
MODEL_UNAVAILABLE when it doesn't answer; CONVERSATION_TOO_LONG when
the conversation won't fit the chat's context window. A question that
isn't about Vennir gets the same short answer (off_topic), and an
answer from neither the docs nor the platform isn't shown (uncited).

methods.name: AskStream
methods.comment:
Ask, with each step as it's taken (a tool used, whether it worked),
then the answer. The answer's words come only at the end, checked:
what the model says isn't shown until the console has checked it.

methods.name: GetChatConfig
methods.comment:
The chat agent's model as it's set: the install's (the chart's chat
values) or an admin's. Admins only. Never the key.

methods.name: SetChatConfig
methods.comment:
An admin's own settings, checked as the install's are
(BAD_CHAT_SETTINGS), in effect on every console within seconds.

methods.name: ResetChatConfig
methods.comment: Back to the install's settings; the admins' are forgotten, key and all.

methods.name: TestChatConfig
methods.comment:
Settings tried before they're saved: one real question through the
agent, as the admin. Says whether the model answered, not what another
server said.

methods.name: GetChatLimits
methods.comment:
How many questions each person may ask: by default 30 an hour and 200
a day. Admins only.

methods.name: SetChatLimits
methods.comment: An admin's own limits (BAD_CHAT_LIMITS), for every console at once.

methods.name: RateAnswer
methods.comment:
Thumbs up or down on an answer you got, sent with its question and
answer, for the admins (kept 90 days).

methods.name: ListChatFeedback
methods.comment: The ratings, newest first, at most 200. Admins only.

services.name: DraftService
services.comment:
Compose's drafts: templates being built, kept by the console for the team
each is for, so its members (and admins) see and change them from any
device. A draft is the page's own state, which the console keeps as it
is (at most 64 KiB, 100 a team). Each save names the version it changed,
so two people's edits never silently overwrite each other.

methods.name: ListDrafts
methods.comment:
The drafts of a team, or of every team you're in (every team, for an
admin), newest first.

methods.name: SaveDraft
methods.comment:
Saves a draft: a new one with version 0, else the version it changed.
Refused (failed_precondition, DRAFT_CHANGED) when someone saved it
since, or a new one's name is taken; the Failure carries the current
version.

methods.name: DeleteDraft
methods.comment: Deletes a draft.

services.name: ExecutionService
services.comment:
Executions: DAGs submitted to run, their tasks, events and logs.
Everything here is checked against the caller's teams first: an
execution is visible to a member of any team it names, and changed only
by a member of every one, or by whoever submitted it (a consumer's run of
another team's template, TemplateService).

methods.name: ListExecutions
methods.comment: Executions the caller can see, newest first.

methods.name: SubmitExecution
methods.comment:
Submits a DAG. Each task is checked before anything runs: its team is
the caller's, it runs as its product's ServiceAccount (or "default",
with no secrets, when it isn't a registered product), each secret is
registered for its team, and its image comes from an allowed source,
resolves to a digest and passed its scan. Problems come back together,
as invalid_argument with Problem details.

methods.name: GetExecution
methods.comment: An execution and its tasks, as they are now.

methods.name: WatchExecution
methods.comment:
The execution as it is now, then again each time it changes, until it
finishes or the caller stops listening.

methods.name: ListExecutionEvents
methods.comment: The execution's event log, oldest first, a page at a time.

methods.name: GetExecutionLogs
methods.comment: What each task printed, credential shapes redacted.

methods.name: CancelExecution
methods.comment: Cancels an execution. Cancelling one already cancelled changes nothing.

methods.name: RetryTask
methods.comment: Gives a failed task one more attempt, resuming its execution.

methods.name: RerunExecution
methods.comment:
Runs the same DAG again as a new execution, checked again against the
caller's current teams and secrets.

methods.name: DecideApproval
methods.comment:
Approves or declines a step awaiting approval. Only a maintainer of the
step's team may, and never whoever submitted the run. Declined, the step
fails with APPROVAL_DECLINED, failing its execution; approved, it runs,
and stays approved if it's retried.

methods.name: PreviewStep
methods.comment:
What a step waiting for an approval would do, for whoever may decide on
it: a run (a preview) of its product's plan action with the inputs it
will get.

methods.name: ListPendingApprovals
methods.comment:
The steps awaiting approval in the teams the caller maintains (every
team, for an admin), the longest waiting first.

services.name: GuideService
services.comment: The guides the console shows (console/docs/). Anyone signed in.

methods.name: ListGuides
methods.comment:
Every guide, in reading order: its id and title; then the platform's
own docs (section "reference": architecture, operations, the security
model, the catalog's guide).

methods.name: GetGuide
methods.comment: One guide, as markdown.

methods.name: GetGuideImage
methods.comment:
A figure a reference doc draws (docs/architecture/*.svg, copied with
the docs), by its path from the docs: architecture/6-the-pieces.svg.

methods.name: SearchGuides
methods.comment:
The sections of the guides and reference docs that best match a
question's words, best first: what the chat agent answers from.

services.name: ImageService
services.comment:
Where task images may come from, and their security scans. The cluster
enforces both: the image policy refuses images from elsewhere, the scan
policy unpinned images and digests whose scan failed.

methods.name: GetImagePolicy
methods.comment: The allowed image sources. Anyone signed in.

methods.name: SetImagePolicy
methods.comment:
Changes them. Send back the version read; a stale one is refused
(aborted). Admins only.

methods.name: ListImageScans
methods.comment: One verdict per digest. Admins only.

methods.name: AcceptImageScan
methods.comment:
Accepts a failed scan, with a reason: the image may be registered and
run again until a rescan finds something new. Admins only.

methods.name: RescanImage
methods.comment: Scans an image again now. Admins only.

services.name: NotificationService
services.comment:
What happened that you'd want to know (the console's notifier.ts): a run
of yours failed or finished, a step waits for your team's approval, the
catalog isn't being pulled (admins). Each is in your inbox, and a team's
are posted to its chat webhook (Slack, Google Chat, Teams) when it has
one.

methods.name: ListNotifications
methods.comment: Your notifications, newest first (at most 50), and how many are unread.

methods.name: MarkNotificationsRead
methods.comment: Marks some of yours read, or all of them.

methods.name: GetTeamWebhook
methods.comment:
A team's webhook, for its members: its host and what it's sent; never
its URL.

methods.name: SetTeamWebhook
methods.comment:
Sets a team's webhook (its maintainers): the URL, kept encrypted and
never shown again, under a host the install allows, and which kinds it
gets.

methods.name: DeleteTeamWebhook
methods.comment: Removes a team's webhook (its maintainers): nothing more is posted.

methods.name: TestTeamWebhook
methods.comment: Posts a test message to it (its maintainers), and says whether it went.

methods.name: GetTeamCallback
methods.comment:
A team's outcome webhook (its members): where each of its runs'
outcomes is posted as signed JSON, for its own systems; its host and
last post, never the URL.

methods.name: SetTeamCallback
methods.comment:
Sets it (its maintainers), under the install's allowed hosts; an empty
url removes it. Its signing secret is returned when it's first set or
rotated, and never again.

methods.name: GetAdminChannel
methods.comment:
The admins' chat channel: the team whose webhook may also get admins'
alerts (platform_alert, catalog_failing, and every team's step_refused).
Admins only.

methods.name: SetAdminChannel
methods.comment: Chooses it (a team's name), or none (empty). Admins only.

methods.name: GetEmailPreferences
methods.comment:
Which of your notifications are emailed to you too, and whether this
install sends email at all.

methods.name: SetEmailPreferences
methods.comment:
Chooses which kinds are emailed to you (any of run_failed,
run_succeeded, approval_waiting, product_not_ready, catalog_failing,
step_refused, platform_alert, api_access).

services.name: ObserveService
services.comment:
Observe: what this install checks, what it refused, and what everything
is doing. Everyone signed in sees the security checks (what's enforced,
what's refused, every image that may run and its scan); runs' details
follow who may see each run.

methods.name: GetSecurity
methods.comment:
What this install enforces (and what it doesn't yet), what it refused
over the last week, and every image allowed to run here.

methods.name: GetImageSbom
methods.comment:
An image's software bill of materials (CycloneDX JSON), as catalog CI
attached it, signed by the image's signer; for an image the caller may
see. NOT_FOUND when it has none.

methods.name: GetMetrics
methods.comment:
What the steps are doing: started and how long they waited, hour by
hour over the last day; why they failed; and each product's step
times over the last week.

methods.name: GetUsage
methods.comment:
Who ran what over the last day, week or month: runs started for each
team, who started them, the products their steps used, and the teams
each team's products ran for. From the console's own record of runs,
read at most once a minute. Admins see every team; anyone else the
teams they're in, their products' users, and their teams' use of
others' products.

methods.name: ListAlerts
methods.comment:
The install's alerts, as the Prometheus the console reads has them now
(the console chart's monitoring.prometheusUrl, else the bundled one):
the charts' rules (groups vennir-*), each inactive, pending or firing,
with what it fires for. Everyone signed in; a firing instance about an
API the caller can't see is counted, not described.

methods.name: ListAudit
methods.comment:
Who changed what, newest first. Admins see every entry; anyone else
their own, and what was done to their teams and to runs in them.

methods.name: GetAuditCopy
methods.comment:
The audit log's write-once copy: whether this install keeps one, how
far it has gone, and whether the entries' hash chain held when they
were copied. Where it goes is for admins only.

methods.name: SearchLogs
methods.comment:
Searches the logs kept in Loki (when the install collects them), newest
first. A step's INFO lines reach anyone who may see its run; its other
lines its own team; the platform's own logs admins only. failed_precondition
(LOGS_OFF) when this install doesn't collect logs.

services.name: OrderService
services.comment:
The order builder (decision 23): a cart of actions made into one run's
steps, each input wired by its wiring type (an input's x-vennir-needs to
the one output in the cart whose x-vennir-provides is the same), for
Compose to open. It never runs anything: a person reviews the result in
Compose and runs it, or proposes it as a template.

methods.name: PreviewOrder
methods.comment:
Wires a cart (decision 25). Each required input whose type no step
provides is offered what the team (or you) already has of it, none
chosen (CHOOSE_EXISTING, with "a new one" when the type has a default
provider); with nothing there, the type's default provider is added
(when the catalog names one), or, for a shared type, one parameter is
asked once. An input of a type its own action provides (what it makes)
is yours to fill. An optional input nothing fills is suggested
(`suggestions`), not added. An input two outputs could fill is left for
you to choose (AMBIGUOUS, with the options), unless `choices` says
which; a cycle is reported (CYCLE). Members of `team` (and admins); an
ordering bot may not (ORDERS_ONLY).

methods.name: PlaceOrder
methods.comment:
Places a cart as one run for `team` (decision 25): planned as
PreviewOrder plans it, with `choices` made and `values` given. Refused
while a choice is unmade, or a required value without a provider is
missing (ORDER_INCOMPLETE, with what's left in the Failure detail).
Each step runs as its action would alone: shared with you for the team,
its targets ones the team may use, its inputs fitting its schema (a
value another step gives, targets included, checked once known). The
run is the team's, and an order (its template "order", its cart as its
parameters). Members of `team` (and admins); an ordering bot may not.

services.name: ProductService
services.comment:
Products: reviewed images and their actions, registered from the catalog.
A product name and an image repository belong to the first team that
registers them, the repository even after its products are deleted.

methods.name: ListProducts
methods.comment: Every product the caller may see: all but other teams' hidden ones.

methods.name: RegisterProduct
methods.comment:
Registers or updates a product: an admin, or a token with
products:register (the catalog's release); a team's maintainers don't.
With no team it's a platform product: admins only. Refused
(already_exists) when another team owns its name or its image
repository.

methods.name: CheckProduct
methods.comment:
Runs a product's check now (product.yaml's check): its team's members,
and admins. started is false when one is already under way.

methods.name: DeleteProduct
methods.comment:
Unregisters a product: an admin, or a token with products:register.
Its name and image repository stay its team's.

methods.name: ListImageRepositories
methods.comment: Which team owns each image repository. Admins only.

methods.name: ReleaseImageRepository
methods.comment:
Lets any team register a repository next. Refused while a registered
product uses it. Admins only.

methods.name: ListWiringTypes
methods.comment: The catalog's wiring types: what inputs can need and outputs provide.

methods.name: ReplaceWiringTypes
methods.comment:
Replaces every wiring type, for an install whose catalog has no
teams/<team>/types.yaml (a catalog release that has them replaces them
itself). An admin, or a token with products:register.

services.name: ResourceService
services.comment:
What runs made, and deleting it (decision 21, docs/assessment.md). A step
reports what it made or changed as `resources` in its outputs, each
{type, id, name, link}; the console keeps them, with the step's inputs
and outputs, once its run finishes, so they can be deleted after the
run is gone. You see what was made for your teams, by your teams'
products, or by you; you delete what was made for your teams or by you.

methods.name: ListResources
methods.comment:
What you may see, newest first, at most 200: a run's, a team's, or
those matching a search.

methods.name: DeleteResources
methods.comment:
Deletes resources made for one team: a run of their products' cleanup
actions (product.yaml's cleanup), newest first and anything depending on
another of them before it, for that team. Each is deleted once its step
succeeds. Refused with HAS_DEPENDENTS while other resources still depend
on them: the delete is recorded as a request (its id in the Failure
detail's requestId) and the admins are alerted; it runs once one
approves it.

methods.name: DeleteRunResources
methods.comment:
Deletes what a run made that's still there, in the reverse of the
order it was made.

methods.name: ListDeleteRequests
methods.comment:
Deletes waiting for an admin because others depended on them, and the
recent decisions: every one for an admin, else your own.

methods.name: DecideDeleteRequest
methods.comment: Approves a waiting delete (it runs now, as yours) or denies it. Admins only.

services.name: ScheduleService
services.comment:
A team's schedules: a template or action run on a cron, with set
parameters, for the team, as one of its bots. Checked as that bot when
made or changed, and again on every run. The team's members see them;
its maintainers (and admins) make, change and delete them. At most one
run every five minutes.

methods.name: ListSchedules
methods.comment: A team's schedules, by name.

methods.name: CreateSchedule
methods.comment:
Makes a schedule: refused (invalid_argument, BAD_SCHEDULE) for a cron or
time zone that can't be read, one more often than every five minutes, a
bot that isn't the team's, or what the bot couldn't run.

methods.name: UpdateSchedule
methods.comment:
Changes a schedule: pausing or resuming it, its times, its parameters
or its bot.

methods.name: DeleteSchedule
methods.comment: Deletes a schedule. Its runs stay.

services.name: SecretService
services.comment:
A team's secrets: registered by name, their values written straight into
the team's namespace (pasted) or synced from its vault (External Secrets
Operator). Values are never stored by the console or returned by it.
Any of the team's registered products may mount any of them, when a task
lists it in secret_refs.

methods.name: ListSecrets
methods.comment: A team's secrets: names and key names, never values.

methods.name: ListSecretStores
methods.comment: Where a team's secrets can come from: its SecretStores.

methods.name: PutSecret
methods.comment: Adds or replaces a pasted secret.

methods.name: SyncSecret
methods.comment:
Syncs a secret from one of the team's SecretStores: only the reference
goes through the console; the value goes from the vault to the namespace.

methods.name: RevokeSecret
methods.comment:
Removes the registration and what the console created. Tasks already
running keep what they mounted.

methods.name: GetSecretSources
methods.comment: What the "connect a source" guide needs to know about this install.

services.name: SsoService
services.comment:
Single sign-on, as admins set it up: the OpenID Connect provider people
may sign in with (optional: passwords keep working), where their groups
come from, and which groups make whom a member of which team. A provider
the install set (the console chart's sso) is used as it is and shown
read-only here; the groups and their mappings are always admins'. A
mapped team's members who sign in with single sign-on follow their
groups at each sign-in: added, given the mapping's role, or removed.
Admins only.

methods.name: GetSsoSettings
methods.comment:
The provider in effect (the install's, or the saved one) and where
groups come from; never the client secret.

methods.name: SetSsoSettings
methods.comment:
Sets the provider (refused, failed_precondition SSO_SET_BY_INSTALL, when
the install set one) and where groups come from. The issuer's discovery
document must be readable; a client secret left empty keeps the stored
one.

methods.name: ListSsoGroupMappings
methods.comment: Which groups make whom a member of which team, by group.

methods.name: SetSsoGroupMapping
methods.comment:
Maps a group to a team, as member or maintainer; the same group and
team again changes its role.

methods.name: DeleteSsoGroupMapping
methods.comment: Unmaps it. Memberships it gave change at each person's next sign-in.

services.name: TeamService

methods.name: ListTeams
methods.comment: Every team. Admins only.

methods.name: GetTeam
methods.comment:
A team's record and lifecycle. Anyone who may not see it gets
not_found, as for a team that doesn't exist. A purged team is still
returned, with deleted_at: its name stays reserved.

methods.name: GetTeamProfile
methods.comment:
What anyone signed in may know of a team (its page, for those not in
it): where to ask it (team.yaml's contact and help), whether it's
retired, and how many people are in it. Never its members, secrets or
runs. not_found for no such team, or a purged one.

methods.name: ListTeamSummaries
methods.comment:
Every team's owner, description, people and Pods running now, for an
admin's list of teams: one call, not a profile and a Pod list for each.
Admins only.

methods.name: CreateTeam
methods.comment: Creates a team and its namespace. Admins, or a token with teams:create.

methods.name: EnsureTeam
methods.comment:
Makes sure a team exists and is active, with its namespace: creates
it, or un-retires it, any number of times. A purged team's name is
refused (already_exists, NAME_RESERVED).

methods.name: RetireTeam
methods.comment: Read-only from now on, its products unlisted. Reversible.

methods.name: UnretireTeam
methods.comment:
Undoes a retire (its catalog folder restored): writable again, its
products registered again on the catalog's next CI run.

methods.name: PurgeTeam
methods.comment:
Irreversible: a retired team, with no unfinished executions, is
soft-deleted so its name stays reserved. Its namespace is deleted only
where the console may purge namespaces (off by default).

methods.name: ListMembers
methods.comment: The team's members, bots included.

methods.name: AddMember
methods.comment:
Adds someone with an account, as a member unless role says otherwise.
A maintainer's (or an admin's). At most 30 an hour per caller. An
account that signed itself up, never verified by single sign-on, is
refused unless an admin adds it (failed_precondition, EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED).

methods.name: RemoveMember
methods.comment:
A maintainer's. Never the team's last maintainer (failed_precondition,
LAST_MAINTAINER).

methods.name: SetMemberRole
methods.comment:
Makes someone a maintainer or a member: a maintainer's. Never leaves
the team without a maintainer (failed_precondition, LAST_MAINTAINER).

methods.name: SetTeamSignIn
SetTeamQuota
methods.comment:
Sets what the team's steps may use together (written to its namespace
at once), or with use_default the install's limits again. Admins only.

methods.name: ApplySecretStore
methods.comment:
Applies the team's reviewed SecretStore file: only SecretStores in its
namespace, credentials only from eso-auth, and ESO's own
ServiceAccounts; anything else is refused with every problem listed.

methods.name: SetSecretStoreCredential
methods.comment:
Sets the stored credential the team's SecretStores may use (a vault
provider's token): the Secret eso-auth, which no step can mount. This
install's own: the catalog carries the stores, never their credential.
A member of the team, or an admin.

methods.name: ListPods
methods.comment: What's running in the team's namespace.

services.name: TemplateService
services.comment:
Templates: what a consumer runs, filling in only parameters. A template
comes from a team's catalog (dags/*.yaml of kind Template); each step
names an action, and runs that action's product as its ServiceAccount,
with that action's own secrets, in its team's namespace: none of which
the person running it chooses. Every shared action can also be run on its
own, as a one-step template whose parameters are its inputs.

Anyone signed in may run what's shared with them: a template's own team,
the teams it lists in share_with, or everyone ("*"). Whoever runs one may
see, cancel, retry and rerun that run (ExecutionService), as may members
of the teams its steps ran in.

methods.name: ListTemplates
methods.comment:
Every template and action the caller may see: those shared with them,
and the rest (shared = false, with ask_for_access_url) except hidden
ones, which only their own team sees.

methods.name: RunTemplate
methods.comment:
Runs a template with these parameters. They're checked against its
parameter schema first; problems come back together, as
invalid_argument with Problem details.

methods.name: RunAction
methods.comment: Runs one shared action with these inputs, as a one-step template.

methods.name: PreviewTemplate
methods.comment:
What running a template with these parameters would do, without doing
it: a run (a preview) of its steps' plan actions (product.yaml's plan),
side by side, for the steps that have one and whose inputs are known
before anything runs. Each step's outputs say what it would change.

methods.name: PreviewAction
methods.comment: What running one action with these inputs would do: a run of its plan action.

services.name: TokenService

methods.name: ListBots
methods.comment: A team's bots and their tokens (never the tokens themselves).

methods.name: CreateBotToken
methods.comment: Creates a bot, or a new token for an existing one.

methods.name: CreateKeylessBot
methods.comment:
Creates a bot that signs in only from CI, keyless (its team's
maintainers): with no token, and the identity AddBotIdentity would add.
The identity is checked first, so a refused one makes no bot.

methods.name: SetBotOrders
methods.comment:
Sets the templates an ordering bot may order (its team's maintainers):
<team>/<name> each; it may run nothing else.

methods.name: SetBotCallback
methods.comment:
Sets where an ordering bot's orders' outcomes are posted, signed (its
team's maintainers), under the install's allowed hosts; an empty url
removes it. Its signing secret is returned when it's first set or
rotated, and never again.

methods.name: ListBotIdentities
methods.comment:
A team's bots' keyless identities (its members), and what this install
accepts: its issuers and audience.

methods.name: AddBotIdentity
methods.comment:
Lets a bot sign in with a CI's ID token carrying these exact claims, from
an issuer the install allows (its team's maintainers). The claims name
what the token is for (GitHub: repository; GitLab: project_path), and
may narrow it (ref, environment). No patterns.

methods.name: RemoveBotIdentity
methods.comment: Stops a keyless identity signing in (its team's maintainers).

methods.name: RevokeToken
methods.comment: Revokes any token: a team's bot's (by a member) or any (by an admin).

methods.name: ListAutomationTokens
methods.comment: Automation tokens. Admins only.

methods.name: CreateAutomationToken
methods.comment: For platform automation such as the catalog's CI. Admins only.

services.name: UserService
services.comment: People's accounts. Admins only.

methods.name: ListUsers
methods.comment: Every person's account (bots are listed with their teams instead).

methods.name: CreateUser
methods.comment:
Creates an account with its teams; returns a temporary password,
shown once.

methods.name: DeleteUser
methods.comment: Its executions stay in the history.

methods.name: SetAdmin
methods.comment:
Makes someone a Vennir admin, or takes it away. Never a bot
(invalid_argument).

methods.name: ResetPassword
methods.comment:
Sets someone's password and ends their sessions; hand it over out of
band. Not for a bot, which has no password.

fields.name: version
fields.comment: The console's image tag, such as 0.4.0; "development" when built locally.

fields.name: environmentLabel
fields.comment: ENVIRONMENT_LABEL: the name the sidebar shows.

fields.name: ssoProvider
fields.comment: Single sign-on's provider ("Google"), or empty when it's off.

fields.name: logs
fields.comment: Log search (Loki), and for how many days back.

fields.name: auditCopy
fields.comment: The audit log's write-once copy.

fields.name: gateway
fields.comment: The API gateway.

fields.name: catalog
fields.comment: A catalog release is read, and whether its signature is checked.

fields.name: scanning
fields.comment: Every image is scanned before it runs.

fields.name: runRetentionDays
fields.comment: How long runs' records are kept.

fields.name: catalogVersion
fields.comment:
Which catalog releases are applied: latest, newest (the newest vX.Y.Z)
or one version; empty with no catalog.

fields.name: catalogPollSeconds
fields.comment: How often the console looks for a new release, in seconds.

fields.name: catalogSignerKeys
fields.comment:
Who may sign a release: how many public keys are trusted, and a
keyless identity's issuer and subject pattern (empty: none).

fields.name: externalCatalog
fields.comment:
Another install's catalog, read from its registry, as the install is
configured (vennir.yaml's externalCatalog; nothing the console reads
confirms it); empty when this install's own (or none).

fields.name: email
fields.comment:
Email: whether it's sent, through which SMTP host, from which address.
Never its credentials.

fields.name: monitoringProvider
fields.comment: Prometheus: operator, google or bundled; empty when monitoring is off.

fields.name: grafanaUrl
fields.comment: Where the install's Grafana is, for its dashboard; empty when unknown.

fields.name: sessionLength
fields.comment: How long a session lasts before signing in again: 8h, 30m, 1d.

fields.name: auditKeepDays
fields.comment:
The audit copy's bucket: how many days it keeps each copy (0: not
known here), and whether that retention is locked, as the install is
configured (vennir.yaml's audit.keepDays and audit.lock). The bucket
enforces them; the console can't read them back from it.

fields.name: policySyncSeconds
fields.comment: How often the cluster policies are rewritten whatever changed, in seconds.

fields.name: imageSignaturesRequired
fields.comment:
Catalog images run only if signed: whether the kernel chart's signature
policy (a policy-controller ClusterImagePolicy) exists in the cluster.
Unset when the console couldn't tell.

fields.name: rescanHours
fields.comment: Images in use are scanned again once their verdict is this old, in hours.

fields.name: release
fields.comment: Where the release is read from; empty when no catalog is configured.

fields.name: digest
fields.comment:
The release last applied: its digest, its catalog commit, its
repository, when.

fields.name: problems
fields.comment: What applying it couldn't do, one item at a time.

fields.name: checkedAt
fields.comment: The last look, and why it failed (nothing was applied then).

fields.name: newestVersion
fields.comment:
Whether it follows the newest version (a vX.Y.Z tag) instead of
release's own tag, and the version applied, when it was one.

fields.name: applied
fields.comment:
What the applied release held; unset before one was applied (or by a
console older than this field).

vennir.console.v1.CatalogCounts.name: CatalogCounts
vennir.console.v1.CatalogCounts.comment: What a catalog release held: what it applied, problems aside.

fields.name: products
fields.comment: Products by image, each with one or more actions.

fields.name: item
fields.comment: "product web-site-deploy", "team web", ...

fields.name: adoptableTeam
fields.comment:
Set when the problem is a team the catalog didn't make: its name, for
AdoptCatalogTeam.

fields.name: method
fields.comment: What was called: an HTTP method and route, or an RPC's procedure.

fields.name: target
fields.comment: What it named.

fields.name: status
fields.comment: The outcome, as an HTTP status.

fields.name: before
fields.comment: Older than this entry id; the newest when unset.

fields.name: actorId
fields.comment: Only this account's.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: 100 when unset, at most 500.

fields.name: nextBefore
fields.comment: Pass as `before` for the next page; 0 on the last.

fields.name: route
fields.comment: The RPC's procedure, such as vennir.console.v1.ExecutionService/GetExecution.

fields.name: executionIds
fields.comment:
The runs read: one for a run's page, several for a list (resources,
a log search).

fields.name: teams
fields.comment: The teams whose data it was.

fields.name: target
fields.comment:
What was read, by name: step keys (tasks), secret or store names, a
chat tool. Never the content.

fields.name: before
fields.comment: Older than this read's id; the newest when unset.

fields.name: actorId
fields.comment: Only this account's.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: Only reads of this team's data.

fields.name: executionId
fields.comment: Only reads that included this run.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: 100 when unset, at most 500.

fields.name: nextBefore
fields.comment: Pass as `before` for the next page; 0 on the last.

fields.name: applies
fields.comment: False: there's nothing to write to (not configured, or not installed).

fields.name: outcomes
fields.comment:
By policy (identityPolicy, scanPolicy, ...); a policy missing here
hasn't been synced since the console started.

vennir.console.v1.CatalogPolicies.name: CatalogPolicies
vennir.console.v1.CatalogPolicies.comment:
Who writes the cluster's policies of what the catalog decides: which
digests are a product's releases (as which ServiceAccount, with which
token audiences) and each API ServiceAccount's audiences.

fields.name: writer
release
fields.comment:
With the kernel: the release it last wrote them from
(<repository>@<digest>), and that release's commit; empty until it has
applied one it trusts.

fields.name: catalogSigned
fields.comment: Whether this console's catalog trusts a signer (catalog.signature).

fields.name: gateway
fields.comment:
Whether the gateway is on, and whether the kernel writes its API
ServiceAccounts' audiences too (the kernel chart's catalogPolicy.gateway).

vennir.console.v1.Failure.name: Failure
vennir.console.v1.Failure.comment:
Why something went wrong, in a form a caller can act on: a stable code,
a message for a person, and whether trying again may work. A task's
failure, a product's error, and the details of an error response all
take this shape.

fields.name: code
fields.comment: A stable code, such as TASK_TIMEOUT, IDENTITY_NOT_ALLOWED or TEAM_RETIRED.

fields.name: message
fields.comment: What went wrong, for a person to read.

fields.name: retryable
fields.comment: Whether the same request may succeed if tried again.

fields.name: detail
fields.comment:
More about it, when there is more: the images refused and the sources
allowed (IMAGE_NOT_ALLOWED), a failed scan's findings, the executions
still running (EXECUTIONS_RUNNING).

vennir.console.v1.Problem.name: Problem
vennir.console.v1.Problem.comment:
Every problem found with a request, attached to an invalid_argument
error so a caller can fix them all at once. `field` says where, as a
path such as "tasks[2].inputs.region".

vennir.console.v1.PageRequest.name: PageRequest
vennir.console.v1.PageRequest.comment: One page of a list, and how to ask for the next.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: At most this many items; the method's own default when unset.

fields.name: cursor
fields.comment: A previous response's next_cursor, to continue from there.

vennir.console.v1.TaskResources.name: TaskResources
vennir.console.v1.TaskResources.comment:
CPU and memory for a task's Pod, as Kubernetes quantities ("250m",
"512Mi"). A product's are its tasks' defaults; a task's own win.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: The API: <team>/<name>.

fields.name: group
fields.comment: Exactly one of: a single sign-on group (lowercased), or a user.

fields.name: perMinute
fields.comment:
Requests a minute: the user's, or each of the group's members'. With
default_rate, it's the API's default limit, and follows it.

fields.name: grantedBy
fields.comment: Who granted it (an email); empty for an open API's request.

fields.name: accessRequestId
fields.comment: The request it answered, if any.

fields.name: revokedAt
fields.comment: Set once revoked.

fields.name: revokeReason
fields.comment:
Why the platform revoked it (superseded by a grant made while its API
was away), when it did.

fields.name: awaySince
fields.comment:
When its API left the catalog's release; unset while it's published.
Removed 30 days after.

fields.name: userId
fields.comment: Whom it's for: the person, or the bot.

fields.name: requestedBy
fields.comment: Who asked (an email): the person, or the bot's team's maintainer.

fields.name: decidedBy
fields.comment: Who granted, declined or withdrew it, and a decline's reason.

fields.name: groups
fields.comment:
The single sign-on groups the person offered when they asked (none,
or some of theirs), one of which may be granted instead: shown to the
API's maintainers only, and only while it waits. Never the person's
other groups.

fields.name: groupsReadAt
fields.comment:
When those groups were read (when they asked, or a later sign-in that
read them all again): older than 24 hours, a group can't be granted
from them (GROUPS_STALE) unless Google Workspace confirms it.

fields.name: awaySince
fields.comment: When its API left the catalog's release; unset while it's published.

fields.name: reason
fields.comment: Why: the API's maintainers read it. At most 1000 characters.

fields.name: botEmail
fields.comment: For a bot of a team the caller maintains; empty: for the caller.

fields.name: groups
fields.comment:
For the caller: which of their single sign-on groups (as last read,
while they count) the API's maintainers may grant instead of them.
Empty: none, so they're granted by name. Never for a bot.

fields.name: grant
fields.comment: Set when its requests are open: the grant made at once.

fields.name: group
fields.comment: Approving a person's: grant this group of theirs instead of the person.

fields.name: perMinute
fields.comment: Approving: requests a minute; 0, the API's default limit.

fields.name: reason
fields.comment: Declining: why (required), which the person is told.

fields.name: group
fields.comment: Exactly one of: a single sign-on group, or a user by email.

fields.name: perMinute
fields.comment: Requests a minute; 0, the API's default limit.

fields.name: perMinute
fields.comment: Requests a minute; 0, the API's default limit.

fields.name: reason
fields.comment: Why, for the audit log and whoever it named. Optional.

fields.name: grants
fields.comment: Active ones first, then revoked, newest first.

fields.name: requests
fields.comment: Waiting ones first, then the rest, newest first.

fields.name: shareWith
fields.comment:
From the catalog (shareWith, deprecated): teams whose members and bots
may call it, not revocable here.

fields.name: callingTeam
fields.comment: VIA_TEAM and VIA_CATALOG: the team the gateway counts calls against.

fields.name: group
fields.comment: VIA_GROUP: the group; VIA_USER and VIA_GROUP: the grant.

fields.name: requests
fields.comment: Requests for the caller that wait, or were declined.

fields.name: groups
fields.comment:
The caller's single sign-on groups as last read, which they may offer
in a request; empty while their groups don't count (no group source,
an older single sign-on session, or Google's read over 90 minutes ago).

fields.name: grants
fields.comment: The team's bots' active grants.

fields.name: requests
fields.comment: The team's bots' requests that wait, or were declined.

fields.name: mayCall
fields.comment:
Whether the caller may call it: their own team's, granted to them or a
group of theirs, or shared with one of their teams (access_via).

fields.name: deprecated
fields.comment: Why it's deprecated, and what to use instead.

fields.name: internet
fields.comment:
Reachable from the internet: asked for in api.yaml, and allowed for its
team here.

fields.name: url
fields.comment:
Where to call it: the gateway's address and /<team>/<name>, inside the
cluster and, when reachable from the internet, from outside.

fields.name: endpoints
fields.comment: What its spec lets through.

fields.name: perMinute
fields.comment:
Requests a minute the caller may send (their grant's, or their team's
own limit, else the default); 0 when they may not call it.

fields.name: sourcePath
fields.comment: Its api.yaml in the catalog repository.

fields.name: backendUrl
fields.comment:
The API's own team only: where the gateway forwards to, and how it
signs in there (service_account_token, google_id_token or aws_sig_v4).

fields.name: specTitle
fields.comment: The spec's title and version.

fields.name: askForAccessUrl
fields.comment:
When the caller may not call it: a new issue on the catalog repository,
filled in with what to change, asking its team to share it (opened in
the person's own browser). Empty when it can't be built.

fields.name: problem
fields.comment: Unavailable: what the gateway found, and when.

fields.name: limits
fields.comment:
Each team its api.yaml names a limit for, requests a minute; every
other team it's shared with gets default_per_minute: api.yaml's
default, else (default_from_gateway) the gateway's own.

fields.name: accessVia
fields.comment: How the caller may call it (unspecified: they may not).

fields.name: accessRequests
fields.comment: api.yaml's access.requests: open, approval or closed.

fields.name: method
fields.comment: GET, POST and so on.

fields.name: path
fields.comment: As the spec writes it, such as /orders/{orderId}.

fields.name: openapi
fields.comment: Its OpenAPI document, as JSON.

fields.name: message
fields.comment: What every caller is told until it's resumed. At most 500 characters.

fields.name: hours
fields.comment: 24 when unset; at most 168.

fields.name: stopped
fields.comment:
Answered by the gateway: not in the spec, unfit, over the rate, not
signed in or not shared, paused, held or closed.

fields.name: endpoint
fields.comment: "METHOD /path/{param}", as its spec writes it.

fields.name: invalid
fields.comment: Stopped by the gateway for not fitting the spec's schemas.

fields.name: averageMs
fields.comment: The backend's average answer time, in milliseconds.

fields.name: request
fields.comment: "METHOD /path" as sent (no query): what the spec doesn't describe.

fields.name: team
fields.comment:
"" for callers who weren't signed in; "grant:user" for those a grant
names, "grant:group:<group>" for those a group's grant lets in (no
person is named; no team's name has a ":").

fields.name: peakPerMinute
fields.comment: Its busiest minute, against its limit.

fields.name: closedMessage
fields.comment: Closed by an admin, and why; empty when open.

fields.name: refused
fields.comment: What it answered itself, without forwarding, over the last day.

fields.name: outcome
fields.comment:
blocked, invalid, limited, unauthenticated, forbidden, paused, held,
closed, unavailable, backend_error.

fields.name: mostly
fields.comment: The team with the most of them.

fields.name: message
fields.comment: Empty reopens it. At most 500 characters.

fields.name: page
fields.comment: 100 when unset, at most 500.

fields.name: nextCursor
fields.comment: Empty on the last page.

fields.name: total
fields.comment:
Every active grant, whatever the page: in all, and to groups, people
and bots.

fields.name: waitingRequests
fields.comment: Requests waiting for their APIs' teams, and on how many APIs.

fields.name: label
fields.comment: Shown on every page, such as "local" or "production".

fields.name: ssoLabel
fields.comment:
Single sign-on, when on: the provider's name for its button ("Google").
Sign in from the sign-in page (/api/auth/oidc/start?tab=, the tab's own value). Passwords still work, except for the
members of a team that requires single sign-on (Team.require_sso).

fields.name: cloud
fields.comment:
The cloud this install is on (gcp, aws, azure, kind, existing), as
vennir set it; empty when it isn't known, and every product runs here.

fields.name: token
fields.comment: Send as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

fields.name: maintainerOf
fields.comment: The teams in team_names this person maintains.

fields.name: mustChangePassword
fields.comment:
Signed in with a password someone else set (a new account's, an
admin's reset): nothing but ChangePassword works until it's changed
(permission_denied, PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED).

fields.name: hasPassword
fields.comment:
How they sign in: a password of their own, single sign-on (bound at
its first), or both.

fields.name: retiredTeams
fields.comment:
The teams in team_names that are retired: read-only, so nothing new is
asked or changed for them (not even for their bots).

fields.name: idToken
fields.comment: The CI's ID token (a JWT), for the install's keyless audience.

fields.name: token
fields.comment: Send as Authorization: Bearer <token>, for an hour.

fields.name: email
fields.comment: The bot it signed in as.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: A label for this execution; it can repeat.

fields.name: requestId
fields.comment:
Send the same one again (after a timeout, say) to get back the
execution it started instead of starting another.

fields.name: tasks
fields.comment: At least one.

vennir.console.v1.TaskDefinition.name: TaskDefinition
vennir.console.v1.TaskDefinition.comment: One task of a DAG: one action of one product.

fields.name: id
fields.comment: Unique within the DAG.

fields.name: image
fields.comment: A product's image; a tag is pinned to its digest at submission.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: The team it runs for, and the namespace it runs in.

fields.name: serviceAccount
fields.comment:
Left unset, the task runs as its product's ServiceAccount, or
"default" for an image that isn't a registered product.

fields.name: secretRefs
fields.comment: Secrets of the task's team, mounted at /platform/secrets/<name>/.

fields.name: inputs
fields.comment:
The action's inputs. A value of {"$fromTask": "<id>", "$output":
"<name>"} takes another task's output.

fields.name: timeoutSeconds
fields.comment: 300 when unset.

fields.name: maxAttempts
fields.comment: 1 when unset.

fields.name: submittedBy
fields.comment: The submitter's account id; unset if that account was deleted.

fields.name: state
fields.comment: Unspecified if the kernel couldn't be asked.

fields.name: template
fields.comment:
Run from a template: <team>/<template>, or <team>/<product>.<action>
for an action run alone. Empty for a DAG submitted as such.

fields.name: steps
fields.comment:
How many of its steps are in each state (PENDING, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED,
...); empty if the kernel couldn't be asked.

fields.name: finishedAt
fields.comment: When it finished, once it has.

fields.name: submittedByEmail
fields.comment: The submitter's email; unset if that account was deleted.

fields.name: running
fields.comment:
The steps claimed or running now, by step id; empty once it has
finished (a cancelled run's last steps may still be stopping), or if
the kernel couldn't be asked.

fields.name: schedule
fields.comment:
The schedule that started it, by name; unset when none did, or it has
since been deleted.

vennir.console.v1.RunningStep.name: RunningStep
vennir.console.v1.RunningStep.comment: A step claimed or running: which, and which attempt.

fields.name: taskId
fields.comment: The task's id from the DAG.

fields.name: attempt
fields.comment: From 1.

fields.name: submittedBy
fields.comment:
The submitter's email, "(deleted account)", or "the readiness check"
for a product's check (the console's own run).

fields.name: dag
fields.comment: The DAG as submitted, images pinned.

fields.name: runBlocked
fields.comment: Why retrying or rerunning would be refused now, if it would.

fields.name: template
fields.comment:
For a run of a template (TemplateService): which one, as
<team>/<template> or, for an action run alone, <team>/<product>.<action>.

fields.name: templateParameters
fields.comment: The parameters it ran with, and which of the submitter's teams it ran for.

fields.name: schedule
fields.comment:
The schedule that started it, by name; unset when none did, or it has
since been deleted.

vennir.console.v1.RunBlocked.name: RunBlocked
vennir.console.v1.RunBlocked.comment: Why retrying or rerunning an execution would be refused now.

fields.name: code
fields.comment:
TEAM_PURGED, TEAM_RETIRED, IMAGE_NOT_FOUND, IMAGE_NOT_ALLOWED,
IMAGE_POLICY_NOT_CONFIGURED or IMAGE_NOT_RESOLVED.

fields.name: missingImages
fields.comment: The DAG's images the registry no longer has (IMAGE_NOT_FOUND).

fields.name: disallowedImages
fields.comment: The DAG's images outside the allowed sources (IMAGE_NOT_ALLOWED).

fields.name: allowedSources
fields.comment: The allowed sources, for IMAGE_NOT_ALLOWED.

fields.name: taskId
fields.comment: The task's id from the DAG.

fields.name: attempts
fields.comment: Every attempt, first to last: who asked for it and what acted in it.

fields.name: help
fields.comment:
Once it failed: what that means and what to do, whether retrying is
safe, and whom to ask.

fields.name: approval
fields.comment: Set when the step needs an approval.

fields.name: waitingFor
fields.comment:
While it's ready but waiting its turn: another step with the same
concurrency key (product.yaml's concurrencyKey) is running. The key's
inputs, with their values; unset for a step whose inputs the caller
can't see.

fields.name: waitingForCap
fields.comment:
While it's ready but waiting its turn because its product already has
its most steps running (product.yaml's maxRunning).

fields.name: approvedBy
fields.comment: The email of who approved it, and when; empty while it hasn't been.

fields.name: awaitingSince
fields.comment: While it awaits approval: since when.

fields.name: canDecide
fields.comment: Whether the caller may approve or decline it now.

fields.name: canPreview
fields.comment: Whether they can preview what it would do first (PreviewStep).

fields.name: means
fields.comment: Empty when nobody explained the code.

fields.name: fromOwner
fields.comment: The owning team's words (product.yaml's errors), not the platform's.

fields.name: retry
fields.comment:
"safe" (its product is idempotent), "unsafe", or "unknown" (not a
registered product).

fields.name: team
fields.comment: The team whose step it is, and where to ask it (team.yaml).

fields.name: requestedBy
fields.comment:
The email of who asked for it: whoever submitted the run for a first
attempt, or retried it; empty for an automatic retry.

fields.name: trigger
fields.comment: submitted, retried or automatic_retry.

fields.name: actedAs
fields.comment: The identity it ran as, <team>/<serviceAccount>, and its image.

fields.name: page
fields.comment: 100 when unset, at most 1000.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: Only executions naming this team.

fields.name: search
fields.comment: Only executions whose name contains this.

fields.name: since
fields.comment: Only executions created since.

fields.name: mine
fields.comment: Only the caller's own.

fields.name: nextCursor
fields.comment: Empty on the last page.

fields.name: runRetentionDays
fields.comment: How many days runs' records are kept; 0 keeps them forever.

fields.name: state
fields.comment: PENDING right after a submission.

fields.name: eventType
fields.comment: EXECUTION_CREATED, TASK_STARTED, TASK_FAILED and so on.

fields.name: taskId
fields.comment: The task it's about, if any.

fields.name: after
fields.comment: Events after this id; from the start when unset.

fields.name: nextCursor
fields.comment: Pass as `after` for the next page; 0 on the last.

fields.name: lines
hidden
fields.comment:
Lines held back from the caller (debug, warn, error, plain), and the
team that sees them.

fields.name: executionId
fields.comment: The new execution.

fields.name: approve
fields.comment: false declines it.

fields.name: reason
fields.comment: Why, when declining: shown with the step's failure. At most 500 characters.

fields.name: executionId
fields.comment: The preview run.

fields.name: requestedBy
fields.comment: The email of who submitted the run.

fields.name: canDecide
fields.comment: False when the caller submitted the run: someone else decides.

fields.name: values
fields.comment:
What you fill in: {"<step>": {"<input>": value}}, for inputs nothing in
the order fills.

fields.name: parameters
fields.comment: A shared type's value, by the type's name: {"gcp.region": "us-central1"}.

fields.name: requestId
fields.comment: Sent again (a retry after a timeout), the same run.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: The team it's for: Compose's "for team".

fields.name: actions
fields.comment:
The cart: registered actions (<team>-<product>-<action>, as the
catalog lists them), at most 50. One may be in it twice.

fields.name: choices
fields.comment: Which output fills an input two could, from an earlier answer's options.

vennir.console.v1.OrderChoice.name: OrderChoice
vennir.console.v1.OrderChoice.comment:
How an input is filled: one of another step's output (from_step and
from_output), a resource already there (resource_id), or a new one, the
type's default provider (add_new). Send back one of an answer's options.

fields.name: label
fields.comment: For people: what the option is.

fields.name: steps
fields.comment: In an order they can run in: each after the steps it takes outputs from.

fields.name: suggestions
fields.comment:
Optional inputs nothing fills, and what could: add the provider to the
cart, or choose an existing one.

fields.name: provider
fields.comment:
The type's default provider (a registered action) to add; empty when
there's none you may use.

fields.name: existing
fields.comment: What you already have of it, as choices.

fields.name: product
fields.comment: The registered action.

fields.name: inputs
fields.comment: Every input of the action, by name.

fields.name: added
fields.comment: Added as a wiring type's default provider: it wasn't in the cart.

fields.name: kind
fields.comment:
"step": another step's output; "parameter": asked when it runs (a
shared type's, once, named for the type); "resource": something already
there, its value; "unset": for the person.

fields.name: code
fields.comment: AMBIGUOUS, NO_PROVIDER, CHOOSE_EXISTING or CYCLE.

fields.name: options
fields.comment:
AMBIGUOUS: the outputs that could fill it; CHOOSE_EXISTING: what's
there, and a new one.

vennir.console.v1.ChatLimits.name: ChatLimits
vennir.console.v1.ChatLimits.comment:
Questions each person may ask the chat agent (Ask and AskStream alike);
one more is refused RATE_LIMITED, with Retry-After. Bots may not ask.

fields.name: updatedBy
fields.comment: Empty, and no time, while they're the defaults.

fields.name: perHour
fields.comment: 1 to 10,000 each, and no more an hour than a day.

fields.name: rating
fields.comment: "up" or "down".

fields.name: question
fields.comment: At most 4,000 characters.

fields.name: answer
fields.comment: At most 20,000 characters.

fields.name: steps
fields.comment: The tools it used, in order.

fields.name: comment
fields.comment: What was wrong, or right; at most 2,000 characters.

fields.name: rating
fields.comment: "up", "down", or empty for both.

fields.name: email
fields.comment: Who rated it; empty once their account is gone.

fields.name: role
fields.comment: "user" or "assistant".

fields.name: team
fields.comment: The team they're working for; empty for none chosen.

fields.name: messages
fields.comment:
Oldest first, the question last; at most 40, each at most 4,000
characters.

fields.name: id
fields.comment: As the answer cites it: [S1].

fields.name: kind
fields.comment: The doc's kind: guide, current, operating or history.

fields.name: link
fields.comment: The console's page for it, built by the console, never by the model.

vennir.console.v1.ProposedCart.name: ProposedCart
vennir.console.v1.ProposedCart.comment: A cart for the person to open, check and place: never placed by the agent.

fields.name: choices
fields.comment: What the person chose, of the plan's options (PreviewOrder's).

fields.name: values
fields.comment: What they said to fill in, by step, then input, as PlaceOrder's values.

fields.name: step
fields.comment: A step it took: the tool, and whether it worked.

fields.name: answer
fields.comment: The answer, as Ask gives it: the last message.

fields.name: text
fields.comment:
Markdown, with citations like [S1] kept only when they name a section
retrieved for this answer.

fields.name: uncited
fields.comment:
It found nothing to answer from, in the docs or the platform: the text
says so, in the console's words, not the model's.

fields.name: steps
fields.comment: What it did: each tool, in order, and whether it worked.

fields.name: offTopic
fields.comment:
Not about Vennir: the text says what it helps with, and the model
wasn't asked.

fields.name: contextPercent
fields.comment:
How much of the chat's context window the conversation takes, with this
answer: 0 to 100. At 100 the next question is refused
(CONVERSATION_TOO_LONG): start a new conversation.

vennir.console.v1.ChatConfig.name: ChatConfig
vennir.console.v1.ChatConfig.comment: The chat agent's model, as it's set.

fields.name: source
fields.comment: install (the chart's chat values) or admins (set here).

fields.name: provider
fields.comment: vertex, bedrock, anthropic or openai-compatible.

fields.name: endpoint
fields.comment: openai-compatible's base URL (.../v1), or Anthropic's when not its own.

fields.name: effort
fields.comment: low, medium, high; empty: the model's own.

fields.name: keySet
fields.comment: A key is kept (sealed) or comes from the install: it's never sent.

fields.name: problem
fields.comment: Why an admin's settings can't be used now (chat is off meanwhile).

fields.name: installProvider
fields.comment: What Reset returns to: the install's provider and model, empty for none.

fields.name: bedrockRegion
fields.comment:
bedrock's AWS region (Claude in Amazon Bedrock, as the console's own
AWS identity).

fields.name: maxSteps
fields.comment: 0: the default.

fields.name: apiKey
fields.comment:
Empty: keep the one kept, or use the install's for its own provider.
Ignored on Vertex, which signs in as the console.

fields.name: ok
fields.comment: The model answered.

fields.name: problem
fields.comment: Why it didn't, when it didn't.

fields.name: answer
fields.comment: The start of its answer to the test question.

fields.name: citations
fields.comment: How many sections it cited.

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
Its template's name, and so its file's: lowercase letters, digits and
dashes.

fields.name: body
fields.comment: The page's own state, kept as it is.

fields.name: version
fields.comment: Counts up with each save.

fields.name: updatedBy
fields.comment: Who saved it last; empty once their account is gone.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: Empty: every team you're in.

fields.name: version
fields.comment: The version this changes; 0 for a new draft.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: 5 when unset, at most 20.

fields.name: includeHistory
fields.comment: Design history too (kind "history"): for a question of why.

fields.name: guide
fields.comment: The guide's id, and its title.

fields.name: heading
fields.comment: The section: its heading and those it's under, "Upgrading > Databases".

fields.name: excerpt
fields.comment: About 600 characters of it, from where the words first appear.

fields.name: kind
fields.comment: The doc's kind, as Guide's.

fields.name: id
fields.comment: Such as 03-what-is-a-dag, or reference-operations.

fields.name: section
fields.comment: "guides" (using Vennir) or "reference" (the platform's own docs).

fields.name: kind
fields.comment:
What it is: "guide" (using Vennir), "current" (how it works now),
"operating" (installing and running it) or "history" (design history:
decisions, with proposals and rejected options; it answers why, never
what is).

fields.name: sections
fields.comment:
Its sections (its ## headings), in order: the Docs page shows a long
doc a section to a page.

fields.name: anchor
fields.comment:
The heading's anchor, as the page makes it (GitHub's): a heading used
again gets -1, -2…

fields.name: svg
fields.comment: The SVG's text.

fields.name: exists
fields.comment:
False when the cluster has no image policy (the kernel chart isn't
installed).

fields.name: source
fields.comment: The registry path images are published to (catalog CI's target).

fields.name: version
fields.comment: Send back on SetImagePolicy, so concurrent edits can't clobber.

fields.name: allowed
fields.comment: Every allowed prefix, as the cluster matches them.

fields.name: lastSavedBy
fields.comment:
Admins only: who last saved them here, and when, from the audit log;
empty when nobody has since it was installed (or for anyone else).

fields.name: acceptedBy
fields.comment: Set when an admin accepted a failed verdict.

fields.name: findings
fields.comment: At most 25.

fields.name: kind
fields.comment: vulnerability or secret.

fields.name: reason
fields.comment: 10 to 2000 characters.

fields.name: scan
fields.comment: Unset when scanning is off.

fields.name: kind
fields.comment:
run_failed, run_succeeded, approval_waiting, catalog_failing,
product_not_ready, step_refused, platform_alert or api_access (a
request for access to an API, or a grant, changed).

fields.name: link
fields.comment: The console page it's about, such as /runs/<id>.

fields.name: all
fields.comment: Every one of yours, instead.

fields.name: configured
fields.comment: Whether the team has one.

fields.name: host
fields.comment: Its host, such as hooks.slack.com.

fields.name: kinds
fields.comment:
The kinds it's sent: run_failed, approval_waiting, product_not_ready,
step_refused; and on the admins' channel, platform_alert and
catalog_failing.

fields.name: lastError
fields.comment: Why the last post failed, if it did.

fields.name: allowedHosts
fields.comment: The hosts this install allows.

fields.name: adminChannel
fields.comment:
Whether this team is the admins' channel: its webhook may also get
platform_alert and catalog_failing.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: The team's name; empty: none.

fields.name: url
fields.comment: Empty: keep the one set, and change only the kinds.

fields.name: error
fields.comment: Why not, when it wasn't.

fields.name: available
fields.comment: Whether this install sends email (its SMTP server is set).

fields.name: configured
fields.comment: Whether the team has one.

fields.name: lastError
fields.comment: Why the last post failed, if it did.

fields.name: allowedHosts
fields.comment: The hosts this install allows; empty: none, so it can't have one.

fields.name: url
fields.comment: https://, under the install's allowed hosts; empty: remove it.

fields.name: rotateSecret
fields.comment: A new signing secret, the old one no longer valid.

fields.name: signingSecret
fields.comment: Set only when it's new (first set, or rotated): shown once.

fields.name: image
fields.comment: The image, pinned by digest, as GetSecurity lists it.

fields.name: sbom
fields.comment: The CycloneDX document, as JSON.

fields.name: state
fields.comment:
enforced: the cluster (or the gateway) refuses what breaks it.
off: this install turned it off. not_yet: a known gap.

fields.name: at
fields.comment: When; for the gateway's, the last of them.

fields.name: what
fields.comment:
What was refused: a step (its team and id), the catalog's release, or
calls to an API (the calling team and the API).

fields.name: team
fields.comment: The step's team, or the API's.

fields.name: executionId
fields.comment: The run it was in, when the caller may see it; else empty.

fields.name: source
fields.comment:
Who refused it: step (the cluster), catalog (the console) or gateway.
The gateway's are seen by the API's team, the calling team and admins.

fields.name: count
fields.comment:
How many: the gateway's are grouped by API, calling team, endpoint and
reason over the week; 1 otherwise.

fields.name: detail
fields.comment:
Under it: a step's image, the endpoint called, or the release's version
(else its digest).

fields.name: product
fields.comment: The product's registered name, and its team.

fields.name: image
fields.comment: <repository>@sha256:..., as it runs.

fields.name: scan
fields.comment: pending, passed, failed, error, or unscanned.

fields.name: acceptedReason
fields.comment: An admin accepted a failed scan, and why.

fields.name: ready
fields.comment: Steps waiting to start, and running, now.

fields.name: days
fields.comment: 1, 7 or 30; 7 when unset.

fields.name: since
fields.comment: Where the period starts.

fields.name: teams
fields.comment: Busiest first.

fields.name: products
fields.comment: Most used first.

fields.name: runs
fields.comment:
The runs the caller sees counted once each, however many of the
teams it counts for (a raw DAG across two counts for both): in the
period, in the one before it, and their steps.

fields.name: team
fields.comment:
Empty for runs started for no team. A run counts for the team a
template was run for, or every team of a raw DAG. A team whose
products ran, but that started nothing, has a row too.

fields.name: previousRuns
fields.comment: In the period before, as long.

fields.name: steps
fields.comment: The steps of those runs as submitted, retries not counted.

fields.name: used
fields.comment: Steps of its runs by product, most first.

fields.name: ranFor
fields.comment: Steps of its own products by the team each run was for, most first.

fields.name: product
fields.comment:
The registered product, or the image repository for one that isn't
(or a hidden product the caller doesn't see). A step is a product's
only when it ran in the product's team's namespace.

fields.name: team
fields.comment:
The product's team; for an image that isn't a product, the namespace
its steps ran in.

fields.name: usedBy
fields.comment: Steps by the team each run was for (empty: no team), most first.

fields.name: configured
fields.comment: Whether the console reads a Prometheus at all.

fields.name: problem
fields.comment: Why it couldn't be read just now; empty when it was.

fields.name: source
fields.comment:
Where they're read from: "prometheus" (its rules API), or "google": the
charts' Rules in the cluster, and which fire from Google Cloud's
managed Prometheus, which keeps no instance's own summary.

fields.name: project
fields.comment: With google: the project whose managed Prometheus evaluates them.

fields.name: stateUnknown
fields.comment:
With google: the rules were read but which fire couldn't be (problem
says why); each rule's state is then unknown.

fields.name: severity
fields.comment: Its severity label (warning, critical).

fields.name: summary
fields.comment: Its summary, with what varies by instance left out.

fields.name: state
fields.comment: inactive, pending or firing; unknown when it couldn't be read.

fields.name: hidden
fields.comment:
Pending or firing for something the caller can't see (another team's
hidden API).

fields.name: state
fields.comment: pending or firing.

fields.name: activeAt
fields.comment: Since when.

fields.name: labels
fields.comment: Its labels, but alertname and severity.

fields.name: retried
fields.comment: Some were retried automatically.

fields.name: means
fields.comment: What the code means, when the platform knows it.

fields.name: product
fields.comment: The registered product, or the image repository for one that isn't.

fields.name: before
fields.comment: Older than this entry id; the newest when unset.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: Only what was done to this team (or to runs in it).

fields.name: mine
fields.comment: Only the caller's own.

fields.name: refusedOnly
fields.comment: Only what was refused (a status of 400 or more).

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: 100 when unset, at most 500.

fields.name: nextBefore
fields.comment: Pass as `before` for the next page; 0 on the last.

fields.name: enabled
fields.comment:
False when this install keeps no copy: the log is then only in the
console's database, and its chain is checked by nothing.

fields.name: destination
fields.comment:
gs://bucket/prefix or s3://bucket/prefix; empty unless the caller is an
admin.

fields.name: copiedThrough
fields.comment: The newest entry copied (0 for none yet), and when.

fields.name: waiting
fields.comment: Entries written since, waiting for the next copy.

fields.name: checkedAt
fields.comment:
When the export last looked: each look checks the chain of the entries
it is about to copy.

fields.name: brokenAt
fields.comment:
The entry where the chain broke (changed, or one before it removed or
slipped in); 0 while it holds. Nothing from there on is copied.

fields.name: problem
fields.comment: Why the last look didn't copy, if it didn't.

fields.name: comparedThrough
fields.comment:
The database compared with the copy, entry by entry, a few copies an
hour, round and round (the chain alone misses a change whose hashes
were all rewritten after it): how far this round has gone, and when.

fields.name: differsAt
fields.comment:
The first entry the database has changed (or lost) since it was
copied; 0 while they agree.

fields.name: compareProblem
fields.comment: Why the last comparison didn't finish, or what it found.

fields.name: text
fields.comment: Lines containing this, ignoring case.

fields.name: team
fields.comment: Only this team's steps (or API backends).

fields.name: executionId
fields.comment: Only this run's steps (not with source api).

fields.name: level
fields.comment: debug, info, warn or error; any when empty.

fields.name: source
fields.comment:
step (the default); api, the API backends a team runs (Pods labelled
vennir/api-backend), its own team's only; or platform (admins only).

fields.name: since
fields.comment:
The window; the last hour when unset. At most the install's search
window (searchDays) back: older logs are archived.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: 200 when unset, at most 1000.

fields.name: api
fields.comment:
With source api: only the backend of this API product of the team's
(its Pods labelled vennir/api: <name>).

fields.name: truncated
fields.comment: More matched than limit: narrow the search.

fields.name: searchDays
fields.comment: How far back this install searches.

fields.name: team
fields.comment:
A step's or API backend's team (its namespace); empty for the
platform's.

fields.name: app
fields.comment:
For the platform's: which part (app, gateway, scheduler...); for an
API backend's, its app.kubernetes.io/name or app label.

fields.name: name
fields.comment: <team>-<product>-<action>, as catalog CI registers it.

fields.name: teamId
fields.comment: Unset for a platform product.

fields.name: inputSchema
fields.comment: JSON Schema of the action's inputs, and of what it outputs.

fields.name: serviceAccount
fields.comment: The ServiceAccount its tasks run as, in the owning team's namespace.

fields.name: secretRefs
fields.comment: The team secrets it uses (product.yaml's secretRefs): its bindings.

fields.name: shareWith
fields.comment:
The other teams that may run it or include it in their templates, or
"*" for every team; empty, only its own team.

fields.name: deprecated
fields.comment: Why it's deprecated and what to use instead, or empty when it isn't.

fields.name: tokenAudiences
fields.comment:
Audiences its tasks get a projected ServiceAccount token for, at
/platform/tokens/<audience> (product.yaml's tokenAudiences).

fields.name: readiness
fields.comment:
Whether it's ready on this install, by its check (product.yaml's
check); unset when it has none.

fields.name: clouds
fields.comment:
The clouds of the installs it's for (product.yaml's clouds, else its
team.yaml's); empty, every install.

fields.name: cloudsFrom
fields.comment: Where clouds is set: "product", "team", or "" when neither says.

fields.name: runsHere
fields.comment:
Whether it's for this install (its clouds include this install's, or
